test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 16 Sept 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: What is explicit cost?

options.text: It is the only cost necessary to calculate a profit, as it clearly affects a company's profits.
It is a direct payment made to others in the course of running a business, such as wage, rent and materials.
It represents the loss of profit but does not represent a loss of income.
Opportunity cost is the amount that a firm must give up to use a factor of production.

solution:
The correct answer is __**It is a direct payment made to others in the course of running a business, such as a wage, rent, and materials**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Contrary to implicit costs, where no actual payment is made, **explicit costs are payments made directly to third parties during the process of operating a firm, such as salaries, rent, and materials.**
 
• **Explicit costs are expenses incurred by a firm that is simple to quantify and identify.**
 
• The explicit costs of an organization, also known as **accounting costs, **are noted in its records (accounting ledgers) and appear as itemized expenses on the organization's **financial statements, such as its balance sheet and income statement.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** **Differentiate between explicit and implicit costs:**

 
 

 **S.N.**
 **Basis**
 **Explicit Cost(Rs)**
 **Implicit Cost(Rs)**
 
 

 (i)
 Meaning
 Explicit cost is the term used to describe the real payment paid to oneself for factors of production hired from outside sources.
 The cost of self-supplied factors of production is referred to as implicit cost.
 
 

 (ii)
 Expenditure in cash or credit
 These expenses are incurred, and either cash or credit is used to pay for them.
 These costs are covered by self-provided factors; therefore, there is no payment in cash or on a credit basis.
 
 

 (iii)
 Parties involved 
 Owner and outsiders 
 Only Owner
 
 

 (iv)
 Examples
 Paying employee wages, paying rent on rented space, paying loan interest, etc.
 Interest on one's own money, landowners' rent, etc.
